note: Teaching moves for the AI helper, by misconception tag (and 'default' for a mistake without one). Each tag has up to 3 help levels; each level has 1 to 4 different ways to help. They are instructions to the model in English, never spoken as written: the model says the move in its own simple Hebrew, and the ten checks still decide what a child hears. Kept in the server's config (key tutor_moves) by tools/set-tutor-moves.ps1; they move into the content pack in M9.

default: Warmly invite the child to look at the objects again and try once more, slowly.
Suggest pointing a finger at each object while trying again, calmly.
Say that it is fine to try again, one object at a time, and that you will do it together.
Suggest starting again from the beginning, together, slowly.
Suggest saying each number out loud, softly, while looking at the objects.
Say that we can take our time and look carefully at every object.
Offer to count together, one object and one number at a time, and wait for the child.
Suggest using fingers to help, one finger for each object.
M-CNT-SKIP: Show how to go through the objects in a line, touching each one once, so that none is left out.
Suggest putting a finger on the first object and moving along to the next, so that none is missed.
Suggest touching the objects from one side to the other, in order, without jumping.
Suggest checking that every object was touched, and touching any that were left out before counting again.
Suggest counting slowly while touching each object, and looking for one that got no number.
Say that one object may be hiding without a number, and invite looking for it.
Say that an object was probably left out, and invite counting again from the first, touching each one.
Invite counting again together, with a finger on every object, so that none stays without a number.
M-CNT-DOUBLE: Remind that each object gets one touch and one number, and then we move on to a new one.
Suggest that after an object has its number, we move to a new object and do not go back.
Suggest touching an object only once, and saying its number as the finger lands on it.
Suggest saying a number only when the finger lands on a new object: one number for one object.
Suggest counting slowly, and moving on as soon as an object has its number.
Suggest checking where the finger is before saying the next number: is it on a new object?
Say that one object may have been counted twice, and invite counting again together, moving on after each one.
Invite counting again together, with one touch and one number for each object, and then moving on.
M-CNT-SEQ: Invite saying the counting words together slowly, in order, starting from one.
Suggest saying the numbers like a song, one after the other, slowly.
Suggest saying the counting words in order together, then counting the objects with them.
Invite a slow count with a finger on each object, saying the next number each time.
Offer to say each number first, together, and then touch the next object for it.
M-CNT-CARD: Remind that the last number we say tells how many there are, so we can stop there.
Suggest that after counting, the last number said is the answer to how many.
Remind to give only the number asked for, counting them out one by one, and then stopping.
Suggest counting out the objects one by one, and stopping when the number asked for is reached.
Suggest counting while giving, and stopping at the number asked for, without giving more.
Suggest asking: did I stop at the right number? Then checking by counting what was given.
Invite counting together, giving one object for each number, and stopping at the number asked for.
Invite counting what was given, one by one, to check that it is the number asked for.
M-CNT-SIZE: Invite the child to look at how many things there are, not how big they are or how far apart.
Say that big things and small things each count as one, and invite counting both groups.
Suggest pairing the things one to one: one from this side with one from that side, and seeing which side has some left.
Suggest touching one thing from each group at the same time, so the group that runs out first has fewer.
Count the things of one group aloud together, then the other group, and compare the two numbers.
M-NUM-ZERO: Say that when there is nothing at all, there is a number for that too, and it is called zero.
Invite the child to look again at the empty place and say how many things are in it.
Suggest picturing the things that flew away or were eaten: now none is left, and the number for none is zero.
Tell a very short story where the last thing goes away, and ask how many are left.
Show that zero is where counting starts, before the first one, and that it is a number just like the others.
M-ORD-CARD: Say that first, second and third tell the place in the line, not how many there are.
Invite the child to point at the first one in the line, then the second, then the third.
Suggest putting a small number badge on each place in the line, so that the third place has a three on it.
Suggest walking along the line from the start, saying first, second, third, and stopping at the one that was asked for.
Count the places from the start together until the place that was asked for, and stop there.
